name: C2PA: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity landing page
title: C2PA: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity landing page
answer: This is the landing page of the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity, or C2PA. It says C2PA provides an open technical standard called Content Credentials for publishers, creators and consumers to establish the origin and edits of digital content. The most useful point is its plain description: Content Credentials work like a nutrition label for digital content, showing a content's history that anyone can access at any time. The page also says these credentials can help publishers, creators, news media and policymakers establish transparency.

sections.body: The source is the landing page at c2pa.org from the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity, established as a Joint Development Foundation Projects, LLC, Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity Series. It presents C2PA as a provider of an open technical standard and media verification tools. The page does not state a publication date. Its scope is introductory, covering what Content Credentials are and who they are for, not detailed technical documentation.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: C2PA says it provides an open technical standard for publishers, creators and consumers to establish the origin and edits of digital content. The standard is called Content Credentials. According to the page, Content Credentials ensure content complies with standards as the digital ecosystem evolves. The page describes Content Credentials as functioning like a nutrition label for digital content, giving a peek at the content's history available for anyone to access, at any time. It says the credentials can benefit publishers and content creators, news media and policymakers, and help establish transparency in the work they do. The page also frames C2PA around media literacy, media verification tools, analysis of media content, digital safety, content authenticity tools and content transparency by analyzing the origin of media. It does not explain how the standard works, what it contains, who has adopted it, or what technical methods it uses. The text is promotional and introductory rather than a specification or report. It repeats the idea that C2PA analyzes origin and edits to support digital safety and transparency. The only named organisation is the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity, with a copyright line noting it is established as a Joint Development Foundation Projects, LLC, Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity Series.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numbers, dates or metrics. Its specific claims are that C2PA provides an open technical standard called Content Credentials, that Content Credentials establish the origin and edits of digital content, that they function like a nutrition label for digital content, that their history is available for anyone to access at any time, and that they can benefit publishers, content creators, news media and policymakers by helping establish transparency.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Media would use this source to understand the standards body position that provenance can be handled through an open technical standard rather than invented by each outlet. The page names Content Credentials as the thing publishers, creators, news media and policymakers can use to establish origin and edits and transparency. It is useful as a short statement of intent and vocabulary, not as a guide to implementation. It supports the idea that provenance is being standardised, but it does not give advice for newsrooms or describe how to attach credentials to a file.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Media

sections.body: The page is a landing page with little substance. It does not cover how Content Credentials work, what the technical specification contains, adoption, governance, costs, legal issues or newsroom workflows. It gives no publication date, no named adopters and no examples. It is introductory and promotional in tone, so it should be treated as a statement of C2PA's aims rather than a detailed or independent account.
sections.heading: Limits of this source

source_name: Provenance is being standardised, not invented per outlet
